---
title: "How to use these companions"
---

Use the slides for lecture flow, a companion for explanations and self-checks,
and the selected lab/exercises for practice. You do not need to read duplicate
explanations in every resource. Earlier chapters are for revision; nothing in them is collected or graded.

The approved [syllabus](https://lnajman.github.io/math346/syllabus/index.html),
[workload guide](https://lnajman.github.io/math346/weeks/workload-guide.html) and
Blackboard announcements remain authoritative. Nothing in the companions is
collected or graded. Keep your checked script for your own use and any checkpoint
announced on Blackboard. In-class exits keep their announced classroom route;
solo self-checks need no submission.

## Choose a route

The ordinary-week practice budget is **90–120 minutes total**, including selected
companion reading, lab checkpoints and Core exercises. It is a budget, not a
measured chapter completion time. Assessment weeks use the announced reduced
selection. Guided work is selective; Extension work is optional. A full AI-review
lab is used only when selected, even where a short audit supports a Core exercise.

The first-pass route gives an order for about 30 minutes of recovery. Stop where
you reach and resume later. It does not promise completion of every step or
replace the full Core practice. Student/TA timing has not yet been measured.

## Read / Explain / Check / Interpret

Read what enters the code and what it does. Explain the expected result. Choose
a check that could expose a particular mistake. Interpret the output with its
units, population or domain, and the limits of the check.

**Think first** means a mental prediction. **Private comment first** asks for one
brief comment before expanding a reveal, so you can compare your own reasoning
with the model explanation. Those few comments are private and not collected.
A clean run recreates the calculation; independent known-answer checks help
establish what the calculation means.

## Run the code in the right place

Download starters before looking at possible solutions. TODO comments are
placeholders: an unfinished script can run without completing the analysis.
Keep each MATLAB reference as its own saved script, especially when it contains
local functions. Run R definitions before their first use, including those in
reference reveals. Reading excerpts are fragments; use the complete supplied
script when executing them.

**Printed output in this HTML is an example from a checked run.** It cannot
confirm the state of your computer. Run setup checks yourself, inspect your own
output, and investigate the first failed check rather than weakening it.

## Software compatibility

For MATLAB, Symbolic Math Toolbox is needed in Week 5. The Week 2 helper uses
max(...,[],"all"), a feature requiring R2018b or later; older versions have not
been certified for this material. For R, the native pipe needs R 4.1 or later,
and Week 10 relationship declarations need dplyr 1.1 or later. The current
validation used MATLAB R2026a with Symbolic Math Toolbox, R 4.6.1, ggplot2 4.0.3
and dplyr 1.2.1. The Week 6/8 `$labels` checks pass with ggplot2 4.0.3. This is a tested
version, not evidence that 4.x is the minimum; other versions have not been
checked in this review.
See the [software requirements](https://lnajman.github.io/math346/resources/software-requirements.html)
for the setup route and support.
